about.heading: Architectural Clarity in Modern Jurisprudence
paragraphs: As a second-year student at Columbia Law School, my scholarly exploration and professional focus center on the intersection of administrative governance, commercial dispute resolution, and appellate litigation. I approach advocacy as an architectural craft: discerning the foundational axioms of doctrine, dissecting statutory frameworks, and constructing briefs that withstand intense judicial interrogation.

Prior to legal studies, my academic background in political philosophy instilled a deep reverence for the coherence of the law. At Latham & Watkins and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, I developed hands-on exposure to high-stakes antitrust inquiries and federal motions practice — reinforcing my conviction that clarity, thoroughness, and intellectual honesty remain an advocate's most potent tools.
about.quote: Effective advocacy demands not merely knowledge of the doctrine, but the precision to distill complexity into compelling truth.
